title: Build the mutation journal and kondo trash
why: ADR-0001 makes every mutation reversible, and nothing in the app writes yet. The journal and trash have to exist before the first toggle, not alongside it.
what: Append-before-write journal at <kondo-data>/journal.jsonl, a kondo-owned trash at <kondo-data>/trash/<journal-id>/, and an undo(journalId) workspace method. Ships with the ADR-0001 safety-invariant tests docs/testing.md defers to the first mutation: journal written before the store is touched, undo restores a fixture byte-for-byte, no write lands outside a known store.

title: Introduce the kind registry and capability matrix
why: foundations.md names this as v0.2's structural step. A single boolean write-permission model was enough for skills alone and does not survive five entity kinds.
what: Replace the hard-coded adapter set with kinds that each supply discover, read, capabilities, enable and disable, with identity per ADR-0008. Write permission becomes a capability matrix keyed by kind, scope and operation rather than one flag. The snapshot cache, error isolation and id allow-list skeleton stay as they are.

title: Enable and disable skills through the native convention
why: ADR-0006: kondo speaks Claude's own language rather than keeping shadow state. Disabling a skill means moving it to skills.disabled, which Claude already honours.
what: Move a user-scope skill between ~/.claude/skills and ~/.claude/skills.disabled through the journal, with the scoped equivalent for project skills. Plugin-shipped skills are read-only and the capability matrix must say so. The UI gets a toggle per skill row that re-reads the store after every mutation.

title: Enable and disable plugins per scope
why: A plugin's enabled state lives in enabledPlugins in a settings layer, and today kondo only reports which layers list it. Toggling by hand means editing JSON in the right file.

title: Move a skill between scopes and projects
why: Skills accumulate in the wrong scope and moving one by hand means copying a directory and hoping nothing referenced the old path. This is the feature the tool is named for.
what: Copy, verify, then trash the source, all journaled as one reversible operation. Handles user to project, project to user, and project to project. Refuses a move whose destination already holds that skill name rather than merging, and refuses plugin-owned sources outright.

title: A failed mutation leaves a journal entry whose undo throws
why: mutate() appends the journal entry before any step runs (ADR-0001 decision 5 - an unjournaled write is an un-undoable one), so a step that fails mid-operation leaves an entry on disk describing work that did not happen. journalList shows it as a completed operation, and journalUndo on it throws: undo of a trash step unconditionally relocates from trashPath(original.id, ...), which was never written. Observed while adding the verified copy step in 005 - a move whose copy fails verification is exactly this shape. Entry 007 puts undo in front of users, which turns a throw into something they will hit.
what: Decide and implement what the journal records about a partially-run operation. Options seen from 005: record which steps actually ran (a second append is not allowed - the file is append-only per the 001 lesson, so this likely means the entry carries per-step outcome only via a following compensating entry), or make undo tolerant per step - skip a trash restore whose trash directory is absent while the source is present, and skip a move whose destination is absent. mutations.ts act() already guards the copy and write reversals with exists(); the trash reversal is the one that does not. title: The cached project inventory never notices an external registry write
why: Observed live on 2026-09-03 driving the Leftovers view shipped by entry 040. A dead project entry sat plainly in ~/.claude.json and the view reported nothing left over, because electron/main/workspace/workspace.ts caches the session inventory for the process lifetime behind inventory(). configOrphans reads the registry fresh but takes sources.location from that cache, so a projects[] key added after kondo started is absent from the location map and the loop at electron/main/workspace/user-store.ts:1327 continues past it. dropInventory() runs on mutation only; nothing invalidates on someone else's write, and a renderer reload does not help because the cache is main-side. ADR-0009 makes the registry half the project set and ADR-0010 assumes Claude rewrites it during every session, so this is the common case, not an edge one.
